stated_limitation: Thresholding: Place cell identification uses the 75th percentile of spatial information scores; alternative thresholds (e.g., 80th percentile, fixed information threshold) may yield different classifications.

justification.dataset: Hippocampal CA1 with position tracking does contain place cells, but the in-flight microgravity session, multi-unit records, and noisy tracking make this a harder-than-necessary choice.
justification.handling: Real NWB data are loaded and aligned, but there is no unit-quality filtering and the 2.5 cm binning over a 255 cm arena leaves most bins severely under-sampled.
justification.analysis: The spatial-information metric is miscomputed (unweighted mean rate against occupancy-weighted probabilities), there is no shuffle/null control, and place cells are defined by an arbitrary top-25% cutoff with no significance test.
justification.correctness: Reported information values (mean 34.8, max 136 bits/spike) exceed the theoretical log2(N_bins) bound and are physically impossible, forcing correctness to 0.
justification.figures: The 'top place cell' rate maps show scattered noise with no localized fields, directly contradicting the text's claim of localized firing, and the highest-information units are the lowest-rate noisiest cells.
justification.honesty: The write-up presents noise maps as demonstrated place cells with 'hallmark' localized firing and labels the noisiest low-rate units as top place-cell examples, an unsupported positive claim.
justification.verdict: Physically impossible headline numbers, no visible place fields, and unsupported positive claims make this a reject.
